summary:
Stale re-review at ff666b0, covering two things: the merge of uat into SL-069 (dadcc1b, which brings in SL-071's src/FsAnalyser.Core and Core.Tests changes) and build attempt 6. I found nothing new.

**The two slices together.** SL-071 touches none of SL-069's files: fitness.yaml, ArchitectureRulesTests.cs, eng/, tests/rules and tests/bugs are all untouched. They meet only where SL-069's rules and harness plants reach SL-071's files: Scanner.cs (the anchor for F01-F03 and C-007's stray-violation bite), VolumeSpace.cs, Native/Kernel32.cs and TopLevelRowText.cs. I ran:
- **Fitness op=check** (rebuilt): all 64 rules hold over 109 parsed files.
- **The full harness on the merged tree** (`harness.py --scenario all`, exit 0 in 18 s): clean baseline with xunit 11 Facts and 0 hits, 48 rows all AS-RECORDED, 0 stray hits.
- **The acceptance repro:** exits 0.

**Attempt 6.** Get-ImportRuleNames now passes each name through the same `encode('ascii','backslashreplace')` that the harness's `say()` applies to every line, so both ends of C-007's comparison now use the same spelling. The ImportRuleNames shape builds its é and em-dash probe from [char] values, and both files it touches are pure ASCII (0 bytes above 127 in either). I ran the shape with the engine on the merged tree: exit 0 in 68 s. The copy AGREEs at 11/15/27/58, and C-007 passes under powershell.exe and pwsh with 9 import rules named and none left unnamed. That run also exercised C-007's stray-violation bite against SL-071's Scanner.cs.

**Follow-up worth keeping.** The builder's structural follow-up still stands and would retire this class of finding: have the harness print a machine-readable JSON line of the unran rule names and compare that list directly. It changes harness.py's output contract, so it belongs to a person to rank, not to this review.

Second round: Second lens on attempt 6: one new defect, m6, in C-007's name comparison. A folded name written `name: >` breaks it; that is YAML's default folded form, where the shape feeds only the `>-` variant.

I confirmed it with the real code on both sides of the comparison, not by reasoning:
- Get-ImportRuleNames, loaded from RuleCases.ps1's AST, returns '...never imports Core\n'. yaml.safe_load keeps the trailing newline, and the engine keeps it through `str()`.
- harness.describe_not_run followed by harness.say, imported from eng/rules-harness, prints that newline through Windows text-mode stdout. After Out-String the output holds `'...never imports Core\r\n'`.
- `$run.Output.Contains("'$_'")` is therefore False, and C-007 would list the rule as unnamed on a correct run.

The shape's title, 'however yaml spells its name', is also false for this spelling.

This is the fifth mismatch in the same comparison: two independently produced spellings of one name are matched as text inside a console line. That supports the builder's structural follow-up, a machine-readable JSON line from the harness compared as parsed lists. A narrower patch is also possible.

findings.claim:
An import rule whose name uses YAML's default folded form, `name: >` (clip chomping), fails C-007 on a correct harness run.
- yaml.safe_load gives that name a trailing '\n', and the engine keeps it through `str()`.
- The harness prints the name inside the NOT RUN line. Python's text-mode stdout on Windows writes the '\n' as '\r\n', and Out-String keeps it.
- Get-ImportRuleNames returns the name with a bare '\n', so `$run.Output.Contains("'$_'")` is False and the rule is reported as unnamed.

I ran this end to end. On a yaml with `  - name: >` / `      the provider's folded-with-newline probe never imports Core`, Get-ImportRuleNames (loaded from RuleCases.ps1's AST) returned '...Core\n'. harness.describe_not_run plus harness.say (imported from eng/rules-harness) printed `'...Core\r\n' | CLEAN`. The C-007 check returned False. The same happens for a `|` literal name, or any name that contains a newline.

Shape-ImportRuleNames feeds only `>-`, which strips the newline, so nothing tests this. Its title, 'however yaml spells its name', claims coverage it does not have.
findings.evidence: tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1:703 (`$run.Output.Contains("'$_'")`) and Get-ImportRuleNames just above it. eng/rules-harness/harness.py describe_not_run (the `"'" + name + "'"` join) and say() at :70-72. The only folded probe in tests/bugs/SL-069-EveryCaseFollowsCounts.Tests.ps1 Shape-ImportRuleNames is `>-`. The shape's title is at :511.
findings.fix: Smallest: at RuleCases.ps1:703, compare against the output with its line endings normalised, `$run.Output.Replace("`r`n", "`n").Contains("'$_'")`, and add a `name: >` probe to Shape-ImportRuleNames. Structural, which closes this class of mismatch: the builder's follow-up. The harness prints one extra line, `harness: not-run-json <json.dumps(names)>`, and C-007 parses it and compares it as a list with Get-ImportRuleNames' list.

obligations.evidence: tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1, Get-ImportRuleNames: the python -c now emits `r['name'].encode('ascii', 'backslashreplace').decode('ascii')`, which is the transform harness.py:70-72 say() applies. Shape-ImportRuleNames in tests/bugs/SL-069-EveryCaseFollowsCounts.Tests.ps1 adds a probe name holding [char]0xE9 and [char]0x2014. My run on the merged tree: exit 0, 'the 9 import rule(s) are named NOT RUN ... (unnamed: )' under both hosts.
I re-ran tests/bugs/SL-069-RuleCasesDeriveCounts.Tests.ps1 at ff666b0, after the SL-071 merge: exit 0.
Full harness on the tree merged with SL-071: clean baseline, 48/48 AS-RECORDED, exit 0. C-007 run inside ImportRuleNames passes under both hosts, stray-violation bite included.

drift: The uat merge brought in SL-071's changes to src/FsAnalyser.Core (Scanner.cs, VolumeSpace.cs, Native/Kernel32.cs, ScanOptions/ScanProgress/ScanResult, TopLevelSnapshot/Tracker), src/FsAnalyser.App/TopLevelRowText.cs and Core.Tests. None of it departs from SL-069's design. SL-069's rules and plants were re-measured against it: Fitness holds, harness 48/48.
unreviewed: SL-071's src/ and tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/ changes that arrived with the uat merge: not read line by line. They are another slice's reviewed work, checked here only where they meet SL-069's rules and harness: the full harness run, Fitness, the plant anchors, and C-007's bite on Scanner.cs.
